title: Ramsey number R(7,20), lower bound
statement: Find a two-colouring of the edges of K_n with no red K_7 and no blue K_20; it shows R(7,20) > n. The best known lower bound is R(7,20) >= 920, so a colouring of K_919 exists (built by the construction behind the survey's inequality; none is printed) and one of K_920 or more would improve it.
submission: Text file: the n x n adjacency matrix of the red graph, one line of n characters 0/1 per vertex (1 red, 0 blue), symmetric with a zero diagonal; n <= 2048.
score: n, the number of vertices of the colouring; it proves R(7,20) >= n + 1 (larger is better)

best_known.source: R(7,20) >= 920: implied by item 2.3.h of the survey, R(k,p+q-1) >= R(k,p) + R(k,q) + k - 2 for k >= 5, with R(7,19) >= 908 and R(7,2) = 7; Small Ramsey Numbers rev. 18 (24 Apr 2026) printed blank in Table IIa; read 8 Nov 2026

provenance.keeper: Small Ramsey Numbers (S. Radziszowski), EJC Dynamic Survey DS1
provenance.holder: implied by the survey's inequalities (no colouring is printed)
